nodes.line: Been here since before it was like this. Go on.

It is not a police matter and I have checked. I am sending back 74 papers a day from Bella Vista and paying to have them collected, which is a business model somebody invented on purpose. I am not after trouble. I am after an answer. I'll see you right for it.

Honestly, I am past caring how it looks. They will drop my Bella Vista order if I can show $114 of turnover on the other side of the shop by a public holiday nobody remembered. Nobody else seems to have noticed, which is its own problem. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.
Take a breath. Then say the whole thing.

choices.text: Returns at Bella Vista — that's done.
The Better Rate, Bella Vista — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.

npcs.name: Hemi, paper runner at Bella Vista

nodes.line: Do not mind the mess. It is structural now.

I would do it myself if I could leave the counter. I do the Bella Vista round from the second express and for the last fortnight somebody has been taking the papers off the front steps behind me. Everyone I have told has looked at me the way you are now. Just do not come back empty-handed.

You will think I am making this up. There is a dog on the Bella Vista round that has had two of my bags and a laminated notice that was not even mine. This is the third time I have had this conversation. I will know if you skipped a bit.
Go on then. What did you find.

choices.text: The Bella Vista Round — that's done.
The Dog on Ash Street, Bella Vista — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.

npcs.name: Senna, lotto regular at Bella Vista

nodes.line: If you are selling something the answer is no.

There is no clever way to say this. Nine of us at Bella Vista have gone in on the same numbers since a public holiday nobody remembered and one of us has stopped putting money in. It started small, the way these things do. Say nothing to anyone on the way.

You look like you have twenty minutes. The agency at Norwest closed six months before Bella Vista started struggling, and I would very much like to know what they know. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. Do not make a scene about it.
You came back. That already puts you ahead.

choices.text: The Syndicate, Bella Vista — that's done.
The Other Agency, Bella Vista — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.
Cash only and no, I am joking. What do you want.

It is not a police matter and I have checked. There has been a car in the Glenfield yard since every second Friday with a esky of warm cans on the passenger seat and no owner answering. I am not after trouble. I am after an answer. I'll see you right for it.

Honestly, I am past caring how it looks. Now that it is documented, Glenfield is owed $169 in storage and the only person who can pay it is the person not answering. Nobody else seems to have noticed, which is its own problem. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.
Right. Tell me and do not soften it.

choices.text: The Unclaimed Falcon, Glenfield — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
You have got a face like you can keep your mouth shut.

I would do it myself if I could leave the counter. I am in my first year at Glenfield and I have to log 61 hours on a job I am not allowed to touch on my own. Everyone I have told has looked at me the way you are now. Just do not come back empty-handed.

You will think I am making this up. Somebody has been coming into the Glenfield yard after quarter to six to use the air line, and last week they used the compressor as well. This is the third time I have had this conversation. I will know if you skipped a bit.
I have been thinking about it all day. Out with it.

choices.text: The Air Line, Glenfield — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.

npcs.name: Alfie, the bloke whose car it is at Glenfield

nodes.line: Right. Talk while I do this.

There is no clever way to say this. My car has been at Glenfield since every second Friday and every time I ring, the quote has grown by about $61. It started small, the way these things do. Say nothing to anyone on the way.

You look like you have twenty minutes. The insurance assessor who signs off every job at Glenfield works out of Macquarie Fields, and he has never once seen the car he is assessing. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. Do not make a scene about it.
Well? I can read your face from here.

choices.text: My Own Car, Glenfield — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.
You right there? I am mid-something but go on.

It is not a police matter and I have checked. People leave things at the Mortdale roller door after quarter to six and by morning it is rained on and it is our problem and our tip fee. I am not after trouble. I am after an answer. I'll see you right for it.

Honestly, I am past caring how it looks. The photos worked, which means Mortdale can claim back the $37 we have paid to throw away other people's furniture since the Sunday after payday. Nobody else seems to have noticed, which is its own problem. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.
Sit. Talk. Then I will decide how I feel.

choices.text: Dumped Out the Back, Mortdale — that's done.
The Tip Fee, Mortdale — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.
If you are here about the sign, the sign is wrong.

You will think I am making this up. Two people have been coming into the Mortdale sorting room since the Sunday after payday and taking the good stock before it reaches the floor, and one of them volunteers here. This is the third time I have had this conversation. I will know if you skipped a bit.
You have got that look. Good or bad, out with it.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.
Don't stand in the doorway, mate, come round.

There is no clever way to say this. I do the Mortdale pick-ups in a van with 78 thousand on it and a door that only opens if you know about it. It started small, the way these things do. Say nothing to anyone on the way.

You look like you have twenty minutes. Everything Mortdale cannot sell goes to a warehouse at Oatley, and nobody there has ever answered a phone in my hearing. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. Do not make a scene about it.
Before you start: did anyone see you.
No dramas. Come back when you are bored.
